investigator.note: I prioritized wildfires and flash flooding/waterlogging, as Lahaina experienced a catastrophic 2023 wildfire that killed at least 102 people and destroyed over 2,000 structures, followed by severe 2026 Kona low storm flooding and mud runoff across barren burn scars. For wildfire readiness, I checked access to fire stations, local hospital proximity, animal shelters and veterinary facilities, and tracked land cover changes revealing a jump in bare land from 1.8% to 15.4% post-fire. For flood readiness, I evaluated low-lying block exposure, finding 36.8% of blocks and 3,425 residents in flood-prone areas without nearby elevated building refuges, including two vulnerable schools.

report.summary: Lahaina faces severe vulnerabilities from wildfires and flash flooding following recent disasters that expanded bare land to 15.4%. No major hospital or fire station is mapped within the loaded 3 km area, leaving emergency coverage severely constrained. Key priorities include establishing temporary emergency medical post locations and building flood refuges near vulnerable sites like schools.

calamities.what_happened: A catastrophic, wind-driven wildfire swept through Lahaina, killing at least 102 people and destroying more than 2,000 structures.
Back-to-back Kona low storms brought heavy rainfall and flash flooding to Lahaina, causing mud runoff and road damage in areas left barren by previous wildfires.

readiness.why_it_matters_here: The 2023 wildfire destroyed over 2,000 structures, and post-fire bare ground increased to 15.4% while zero major hospitals or fire stations are mapped within 3 km.

matrix.finding: 0.0% of residents are within 500m or 1000m of a fire station, with median walk distance at 3473m (get_access: fire_station).
No major hospital is mapped within the loaded area (3 km around the place) in OpenStreetMap (get_access: hospital).
1 shelter is mapped within the area serving an estimated population of 9,567 residents (get_area_profile).
0 animal shelters exist in the loaded area, and only 2.7% of residents have a vet within 500m (get_animal_facilities).
No tracked tool data available for animal evacuation during active fires.
Only 1 veterinary clinic (Lahaina Veterinary Clinic) is mapped to treat injured animals post-fire (get_animal_facilities).
Tree coverage dropped from 5.4% in 2016 to 2.7% in 2025, while bare land rose from 1.8% to 15.4% (get_nature_change).
No real-time active fire containment metrics for nature recorded in tools.
Grassland cover decreased sharply from 9.5% in 2016 to 0.1% in 2025 (get_nature_change).

readiness.why_it_matters_here: Post-fire soil degradation combined with 36.8% low-lying blocks leaves 3,425 residents exposed without nearby elevated building refuges.

matrix.finding: 25 low-lying blocks (36.8% of area) contain 3,425 residents, all lacking a refuge within 300m (get_flood_exposure).
Vulnerable educational sites including Princess Nahienaena Elementary School and Lahaina Intermediate School are located in flood-prone blocks (get_flood_exposure).
20 open grounds are mapped that can serve as post-flood emergency staging zones (get_area_profile).
No specific animal flood vulnerability data available.
No data on animal rescue operations during flooding.
No post-flood veterinary response data captured.
Bare land covers 15.4% of the area in 2025 (up from 1.8% in 2016), accelerating mud runoff risks (get_nature_change).
Water bodies cover 12.1% of the area, including Crater Reservoir and Wahikuli Reservoir (get_nature_change).
8 protected area blocks exist to retain natural buffer functions (get_nature_change).

recommendations.what: Construct vertical flood shelters or designate elevated multi-story refuges near vulnerable schools.
recommendations.where: Princess Nahienaena Elementary School and Lahaina Intermediate School
recommendations.why: 25 flood-prone blocks hold 3,425 residents and 2 schools with 0 residents having a refuge building (>=9m or 3+ floors) within 300m.

recommendations.what: Establish temporary medical auxiliary posts and staging locations.
recommendations.where: Mala Historic Wharf, Lahainaluna, and Kelawea
recommendations.why: No major hospital is mapped within the 3 km loaded area, leaving 1,250 residents in Mala Historic Wharf, 918 in Lahainaluna, and 713 in Kelawea without immediate local hospital access.

recommendations.what: Position rapid-response fire suppression units and emergency water supply.
recommendations.why: Fire station walk distances reach up to 5,315 meters in Lahainaluna hexes, and 0% of residents are within 1,000m of a fire station.

recommendations.what: Implement slope stabilization and re-vegetation on burn scars to prevent mud runoff.
recommendations.why: Bare land increased from 1.8% in 2016 to 15.4% in 2025, while tree share decreased from 5.4% to 2.7%.
